name: NVIDIA H200 SXM
memory_bandwidth_basis: HBM3e 5.0Gbps x 6144-bit = 4,800 GB/s (NVIDIA states 4.8TB/s; 141GB = 6 stacks x 24GB on a 6,144-bit bus, which is 6 x 1024-bit = 6,144 bits).
notes: H200 is an H100 SXM with the SAME compute (identical Tensor Core rows: 989 TF32 / 1,979 BF16+FP16 / 3,958 FP8+INT8 printed, all WITH SPARITY - dense is half) and the SAME 700W envelope, but 141GB HBM3e at 4.8TB/s instead of 80GB HBM3 at 3.35TB/s. So H200 is purely a memory-capacity and bandwidth uplift: it wins wherever KV cache or weights do not fit, and loses on nothing. That makes H200 the memory-bandwidth-per-watt inflection point of the Hopper generation. NVIDIA marks the whole table 'preliminary specifications, may be subject to change'. Bus width 6144-bit is inferred from the 141GB/4.8TB/s pair, not printed. The 'other' row is FP64 34 TFLOPS (dense) - this schema's precision enum has no fp64 member.
